question: What is the motto of the Supreme Court of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Yato Dharmastato Jayah**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• "Yato Dharmastato Jayah" translates to "Where there is Dharma, there is Victory".
 
• This phrase is derived from the ancient Indian epic, the Mahabharata.
 
• The motto symbolizes the moral and ethical duty that the judiciary holds in delivering justice.
 
• It is inscribed on the emblem of the Supreme Court of India, representing the guiding principle for the institution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Supreme Court of India**

 
 
• The Supreme Court of India is the highest judicial court and the final court of appeal under the Constitution of India.
 
• It is located in New Delhi and was established on January 28, 1950.
 
• The Supreme Court consists of the Chief Justice of India and a maximum of 33 other judges.
 
• It has extensive powers in terms of judicial review, meaning it can invalidate laws and executive orders that it finds unconstitutional.
 
 
 
• **Other Mottos and Their Significance**
 
 
• **Equal Justice for All**: This is a general legal principle emphasizing that every individual should receive fair treatment under the law.
 
• **Satyamev Jayate**: Translates to "Truth Alone Triumphs" and is the national motto of India, taken from the Mundaka Upanishad.
 
• **Yogakshemam Vahamyaham**: A Sanskrit shloka from the Bhagavad Gita, meaning "I take care of the welfare of those who are devoted to me". It is also the motto of the Life Insurance Corporation (LIC) of India.
